title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): our sentence overturns religion's foundation two ways — precise election without obedience-intuit loves men more than justice and kills all religious solicitude
pass_a_gloss: This being posited they strive to show that our sentence overturns this foundation of religion in a twofold manner. First, because it establishes that God without the intuit of any obedience has precisely elected some unto salvation: whence it follows that God has loved those men more than his own justice: Which being posited, the necessity of rendering obedience is taken away, and all solicitude concerning religion.
pass_b_english: That assumed, they try to show our view overturns religion's foundation in two ways. First: it sets God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze upon obedience — from which it follows that God loved those men more than his own justice. That granted, the necessity of rendering obedience is taken away, and all care about religion.
source_text: Hoc posito conantur ostendere sententiam nostram hoc fundamentum religionis duplici modo evertere. Primo, quia statuit Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: unde sequitur, Deum illos homines magis amasse quam justitiam suam: Quo posito, tollitur obedientiae praestandae necessitas omnisque de religione solicitudo.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. IX Arg. 14 section 675. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap9_arg14_densify.
